requirements.text: The kart is not faster than a speed set for a child.
requirements.design_point: Top speed on level paved ground, with the lightest and with the heaviest rider, is at most kart.speed_max_kmh.
Frame, axles, steering, seat, and their joints carry a rider of rider.mass_max_kg under the load cases of docs/03-design.md without yield or loosening.

requirements.text: The seat and pedals fit a child and an adult.
requirements.design_point: Without welding or cutting, the seat-to-pedal distance and the seat height adjust so that riders from rider.stature_min_cm to rider.stature_max_cm reach the pedals fully and hold the steering wheel with bent arms.

requirements.text: The kart runs on paved ground, gravel or dirt, and grass.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on each of the three surfaces, the kart starts from rest, runs, turns, and stops, climbs site.grade_max_pct, and no part other than the tyres touches the ground.

requirements.text: The kart runs on packed snow and ice.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on level packed snow, the kart starts from rest, runs, turns, and stops, at any speed.

requirements.text: The kart runs in fresh snow.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on level fresh snow of depth snow.depth_max_cm, the kart starts from rest, runs, and turns at any speed without getting stuck.

requirements.text: The kart works in the cold.
requirements.design_point: After standing outdoors at ambient.temp_min_c, the kart starts and runs. With batteries it runs for kart.run_time_min per charge; with an engine it may be refuelled between runs.

requirements.text: The kart is built within the budget.
requirements.design_point: The parts list of docs/05-parts-and-cost.md, with tax, shipping, and winter parts, totals at most budget.parts_jpy, or the owner has accepted the excess.

requirements.text: The kart stops in a short distance.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, from kart.speed_max_kmh on level dry paved ground, the kart stops within kart.stop_distance_max_m.

requirements.text: The drive stops when the driver lets go.
requirements.design_point: The throttle returns to zero by a spring when released, and a stop switch that the driver reaches from the seat, and a helper reaches from beside the kart, cuts the drive.

requirements.text: Moving and hot parts cannot be touched.
requirements.design_point: Chain, sprockets, belt, the turning axle near the seat, and any hot part are covered so that the driver's hands, feet, hair, and clothing cannot reach them from the seat.

requirements.text: The kart slides before it tips over.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, half the track width divided by the height of the centre of mass is at least kart.tip_ratio_min, on every wheel or ski setup.

requirements.text: The frame shields the driver's legs and feet.
requirements.design_point: Seen from the front and the sides, the driver's feet and legs are inside the frame or a bumper.

requirements.text: The kart is carried in a Mitsubishi Delica D:5.
requirements.design_point: With the rear seats of a Delica D:5 folded and slid forward, the kart passes through the tailgate opening (delica.opening_width_min_mm to delica.opening_width_max_mm wide) and lies within the cargo space (delica.cargo_length_mm long, delica.cargo_width_min_mm between the flipped-up third-row seats, delica.cargo_width_max_mm at most), after removing at most parts that come off without tools.

requirements.text: One adult loads and unloads the kart alone.
requirements.design_point: One adult rolls the kart up a ramp onto the cargo floor at delica.lip_height_mm and back down, without lifting the whole kart.

requirements.text: The kart climbs a fairly steep slope slowly without damage.
requirements.design_point: With the heaviest rider, on grass at site.grade_max_pct, the kart starts from rest on the slope and climbs at walking pace or faster, and no part slips, overheats, or deforms.

requirements.text: An adult can set a lower top speed for a small child.
requirements.design_point: Without tools, an adult sets the top speed on level paved ground to at most kart.speed_child_kmh, and the child cannot undo the setting from the seat.

decisions.what: Build one go-kart with one seat, for the owner's private land, to be driven mainly by a child and also by an adult, in summer and in winter. The power source is not preset; the form step compares an engine and an electric drive.

Keep the record public in fujisato-koji/kart, created from the traceable-design template. The record is written in English and the conversation with the assistant is in Japanese. Private facts such as the place stay outside the repository.
The top speed is set for a child, at 30 km/h.
The speed is set for a child, but the strength and the seat and pedal positions must also fit an adult.
The kart runs only on private land, on paved ground, gravel or dirt, and grass. It does not run on public roads.
In winter the kart runs on private land on packed snow or ice and on fresh snow up to 30 cm deep.
The lowest air temperature in use is -10 degC.

The budget for parts and materials is 100,000 JPY, including tax, shipping, and the winter parts, and excluding tools. It is a guideline that may be passed a little; when it is likely to be passed, the assistant names the parts that drive it and the owner decides. The owner would buy a welder if the chosen form needs one.
The heaviest adult who drives weighs 100 kg.
The youngest driver is a 5-year-old child.
On snow the kart may be slow. The top speed of 30 km/h applies on paved ground.
The kart is kept outdoors under a roof, and is carried in a Mitsubishi Delica D:5, in which it should be easy to load and carry.
With an engine, refuelling between runs is acceptable. With batteries, two to three hours of driving per charge is wanted, depending on the trade-off.
The kart must not be damaged on a fairly steep slope. It may climb slowly.
The top speed on paved ground is lowered to 20 km/h, to see whether the kart can be made cheaper.
The tallest adult who drives is about 170 cm tall.

Make the design concrete with new parts that are readily available in Japan, with realistic shapes, and show the designed kart in 3D to grasp what will be built; the 3D view need not be a driving game. This settles item 1 of docs/02-form.md#proposal as new parts (L2). The other items of that proposal are taken as the working basis of step 1.3 until the owner decides them.

open.text: How heavy is the heaviest adult who will drive? The strength is assumed for 100 kg until the owner answers.

How tall is the tallest adult who will drive? The youngest is a 5-year-old (D-010); the lower end of the seat and pedal range is set from the statistics of 5-year-olds. The upper end is assumed at 185 cm until the owner answers.
Does the top speed of 30 km/h have to be reached on snow, or is a lower speed enough on packed snow and in fresh snow? R-05 and R-06 ask only that the kart runs, turns, and stops on snow.
Set the longest stopping distance from the top speed from a go-kart standard or kart rules. Until then it is assumed at 6 m, about 0.6 g.

Set the smallest ratio of half the track width to the height of the centre of mass, so that the kart slides before it tips, from tyre friction data and any standard. Until then it is assumed at 1.5. Also decide whether R-12 must hold standing sideways on site.grade_max_pct, which needs a wider track (form.track_min_slope_m, check K-001).
Where is the kart kept (indoors, under a roof, outdoors), and must it be carried in a car or a truck? This sets the size and mass limits and whether it stands in the cold before a run.
How often is the kart used, and by when should it be ready? The run time is settled by D-013.
How steep is the fairly steep slope of D-014? It is assumed at 20 % (about 11 degrees) until the owner gives a number or measures the steepest slope on the land.

The rough inputs of step 1.2 (kart mass and its rear share, tyre pressure, track wheel diameter, ski size, drive efficiency, tube lengths, ground clearance, heights of the centres of mass, and a mean speed, rolling resistance, electric efficiency, and usable battery fraction for the run time) are assumed so that forms can be compared. Step 1.3 replaces each with the chosen part's data or a calculation.

The price of the 12 V chargers for E2 and the allowances for shipping, small parts, a reduction stage, skis, the track running gear, pedals and cables and the stop switch, guards and mounts, drive chains, and electric wiring are assumed. Whether the snow chain price of M15 is for one tyre or a pair is not known; two are counted. Step 1.5 replaces each with a quoted price.

What is the governed no-load speed of the chosen engine? The gearing for R-01 is set to it. It is assumed at 3850 rpm from a checker's recollection (K-001), not from a source; take it from the engine maker's data, or measure it on the engine when it arrives.

How far does the owner's fresh snow give under a loaded plate? A board of known area loaded to about 5 kPa and to about 16 kPa, set on undisturbed fresh snow and its sinkage measured, settles whether rear tracks (W2) clear snow.depth_max_cm before the frame is given mounts for them.

Should an adult be able to set a lower top speed for a small child? A 5-year-old drives (D-010), while US youth ATV guidance allows no ATVs under 6 and limits ages 6 and up to 10 mph with the restrictor (P25, S2). The child limit is assumed at 16 km/h, about 10 mph, until the owner decides R-17.

The 3D simulator needs the tyre grip on pavement, gravel, and grass, the sideways grip of the front skis, the resistance of tracks in fresh snow, and the resistance when the floor ploughs snow. No source was found; they are assumed so that the simulator can run, and a test run of the built kart settles them. Simulator results that rest on them are illustrations, not verification.

In the owner's Delica D:5, with the third row flipped up and the second row tipped up and slid forward, how wide is the clear space at the floor and at 40 cm above it, and how wide is the tailgate opening at the height of the cargo floor? The sources give only the narrowest and widest widths.
How many hours a day can the owner work on the kart? The plan in docs/data/plan.yaml assumes two to three hours a day for its task lengths.

Step 1.3 assumes, without a source yet, the dynamic load factor on the frame and axle, the density and strength of S45C and STKM11A steel, the masses of a wheel with its tyre, the clutch, the seat, the steering, the brake, the fuel, and small parts, the brake pad friction, and the ratio of buttock-to-heel length to stature for an adult and for a 5-year-old. Cite a standard, a maker's data, or a weighing for each before the gate from design to build.

The parts list assumes the price of steel plate cut to size, of machining by a local shop (keyways on the axle and the jackshaft, boring the 36 tooth sprocket, cross holes for the hub pins, the brake disc carrier), of making the two rear hubs, and of a 25 mm axle shaft of 1.22 m. Get quotes before the gate from design to build.

The fit of bought parts to each other is not stated by their sellers and is checked when they arrive, before the frame is welded to them - the rim's three-hole pattern against the front hubs and the made rear hubs, the front hubs' bore against the 17 mm spindles, the engine's shaft (3/4 inch Q-type) and base holes, the ladder chains on 13x5.00-6 tyres, and the seat's rail bolt spacing.

hazards.text: The kart hits an obstacle, a building, a vehicle, or a person.
The drive keeps pushing after the driver lets go or loses control.
Hair, clothing such as a scarf, or fingers are caught in the chain, sprockets, belt, or turning axle.
The driver touches a hot engine, exhaust, or motor, or the battery overheats or burns.
The kart tips over in a turn or on a slope.
The steering, an axle, the frame, or the seat breaks under an adult.
Braking or steering is lost on snow or ice.
A small child drives faster than the child can control.
The kart rolls off the ramp or falls while being loaded or unloaded.
hazards.at_risk: The person loading it and people nearby.

hazards.text: Petrol catches fire while refuelling or near the hot engine, or exhaust gas builds up when the engine runs in a closed shed.
hazards.at_risk: The driver, helpers, and children nearby.

checks.detail: An independent helper recomputed every claim by hand and then read calc/form_rough.py; the arithmetic held, the method did not in places. Found (1) P1's pmax is the contact pressure, not the inflation pressure, which does not change the conclusion; the sinkage exceeds the tyre radius, and the lowest part is the axle hardware, not the floor. (2) Tracks without road wheels carry the load under the sprocket and idler, so the even-belt pressure understates their sinkage; W2 passing R-06 was not shown, and P1 excludes tracked vehicles. (3) The climb needs rolling resistance on grass and gravel; a motor's force is limited by its controller current; 3600 rpm is P4's rated speed, not the governed no-load speed, so gearing to it may break R-01. (4) Whole teeth and tooth tips put the single-stage sprocket lower still. (5) The track width was rounded down, and R-12 on level ground does not cover the slope sideways. (6) Pedals, cables, stop switch, drive chains, guards, mounts, and electric wiring were missing from the cost, and two snow chains may be counted where one pair was priced. The script and record were changed on each point on the same day; see docs/02-form.md.

A second independent helper rechecked the repairs of K-001 by hand; all seven figures reproduce, and the script matches the record. Partial on the motors - the 2 kW kit's torque, speed, and current disagree (its rated current is probably the controller's rating), the text wrongly said the electric kits climb on pavement, and whether the controllers limit battery or motor current is not assessed. Also noted - the track wheel relation is used beyond its small-sinkage range, tracks on smaller wheels lower the rear axle, E1h has the same margin as E1, and the gearing limits speed only on level ground and uphill. The text of docs/02-form.md was corrected on each point the same day; no number changed.

A third independent helper recomputed the claims after the owner's second answers; every number matched its formula. Partial on what the text claimed - the climb was not checked for grip; the clutch's engagement and lock-up speeds came from two different clutches; a low child limit keeps a centrifugal clutch slipping; climbing at the lock speed is not slow; the overall width exceeded the widest opening only by rounding, and the narrowest opening was in the record but not cited; the battery margin is small; and the donor route left out a new wide axle and brake and treated the donor's ungoverned engine as E1. The record, calc/form_rough.py, and docs/02-form.md were changed on each point the same day; the simulator (with load transfer and rear-wheel spin) shows grip limiting the climb on grass.

steps.action: Check the tyres for damage and their pressure.
Check that the chain and axle guards are on and the chains are tight.
Push the kart and press the brake pedal; the rear wheels must lock.
Work the throttle pedal; it must spring back to idle on its own.
Test both stop switches, the one on the steering and the tether.
Set the seat and the pedals for the driver with their pins.
For the child, set the child speed limit on the governor.
Check that the driver wears a full-face helmet with long hair inside it, and no scarf.
Clear the driving area of people, vehicles, and objects.
An adult starts the engine outdoors with the recoil starter, the kart held by its brake.
The driver sits, clips the tether to the clothing, and holds the steering wheel.
Drive on level ground first; keep to kart.speed_max_kmh, or the child limit.
Climb and descend slopes straight, at full throttle uphill; never turn across a slope.
To stop on a slope, use the brake, not the throttle.
In winter, drive slowly and brake early on snow and ice.
Stop the engine with the stop switch and let it cool.
Refuel outdoors, with the engine stopped and cool, away from children and flames.
Never run or warm up the engine in a closed shed.
Lift the front, take off the front wheels, and bolt the skis onto the spindles.
Fit the chains on the rear tyres and tighten them.
Check the steering moves freely from lock to lock with the skis.
Fold the third row up and tip and slide the second row forward.
Pull the pins, slide the rear hubs inward to the transport track, and pin them.
Hook the ramps on the cargo floor lip.
Push the kart up the ramps, with the engine stopped and the fuel tap closed.
Tie the kart down at the frame with two straps.
